function: Receive combining: estimating transmitted signals from the received multi-antenna signal, robust to scarce pilots and model uncertainty, without needing channel estimation (pp. 1, 3-4).
system: Point-to-point narrow-band MIMO, 4 transmit and 8 receive antennas, 26 radio paths, no RIS; carrier frequency not stated (pp. 3, 11-12).
method: Closed-form distributionally robust linear combiners (diagonal loading, SDP) and kernel ridge regression receiver (kernelized diagonal loading), supervised on pilots; neural networks analysed only, not run (pp. 9-11).
data_channel: Custom simulated multipath MIMO channel: 26 paths, 25 random scatterers in a 500m square; Gaussian signals; impulsive noise on 10% of samples; no standard model (pp. 11-12).
test_conditions: Fitted on pilot blocks of 10 to 100 symbols, tested on 500 non-pilot symbols of the same frame at SNR -10 dB; no new scenario (pp. 12-13).
baselines: Non-learned: Wiener, Wiener-DL, channel-estimation-based Wiener, Capon, Capon-DL, ZF. Learned: only the paper's own non-robust Kernel receiver; deep-learning receivers not run (p. 11).
metrics: Mean-squared error of the estimated signals on test data and training time, averaged over 250 Monte-Carlo episodes (p. 12).
complexity: Measured training time per combiner in Tables I-VI (unit not stated), e.g. Wiener-DR 3.16e+00 and Kernel-DL 5.59e-05 at 10 pilots; no complexity order (pp. 12-13).
q1_support: p. 11: "randomly sample 25 points according to the uniform distribution on the square" to place the scatterers, a custom geometric simulator; no 3GPP, DeepMIMO, QuaDRiGa or COST 2100 model and no measured data is named anywhere in the paper.
q2_support: p. 12: "mean-squared estimation error (MSE) on the test data set (i.e., non-pilot communication data)"; the test data come from the same frame and channel as the pilots, and Tables I-VI (pp. 12-13) only vary the pilot size with each combiner refitted; no new scenario, band, dataset or antenna setting is tested.
q3_support: p. 11: "are not implemented in this section because they have been deeply studied in our previous publications" refers to the deep-learning receivers; the only learned comparator, "Kernel: Kernel receiver (61)", is the paper's own Kernel-DL without diagonal loading (an ablation), so no earlier learned receiver is compared. Wiener, Capon and ZF are compared on MSE (pp. 12-13).
q4_support: p. 12: "Time: The training time averaged on 250 Monte–Carlo episodes" is listed in Tables I-VI for every combiner, including the proposed Wiener-DR and Kernel-DL.
q5_support: p. 11: "All the source data and codes are available online at GitHub with thorough implementation comments", link https://github.com/Spratm-Asleaf/DRRC.
notes: Borderline on the exclusion code no_learning, kept as include: the linear distributionally robust combiners are closed-form designs (Corollary 1, pp. 5-6), but the kernel ridge regression receiver (Kernel and Kernel-DL, Example 4, p. 10) is a supervised model fitted on pilots and gives the lowest MSE in Tables I-VI (pp. 12-13). Neural-network receivers are only analysed (Sec. V-B, p. 11), not run. Area 1 because the task is receive combining that recovers the transmit signals; the abstract mentions ISAC signals (p. 1) but no ISAC beam or waveform design is done. The supplementary material (pp. 1, 12) is not in the PDF, so q1 and q2 rest on the main text only.
